verses.text: Don't brag about tomorrow. You've got no idea what the day will bring.
Let someone else praise you. Let it come from a stranger's lips and leave your own mouth out of it.
A rock is heavy and a load of sand weighs you down. A fool who keeps provoking you weighs more than both.
Fury is cruel and anger can sweep you away. But who can stand up to jealousy?
Open correction is better than love somebody keeps hidden.
When a friend wounds you, they're being faithful to you. An enemy will smother you in kisses.
A person who's full turns their nose up at honeycomb. To somebody hungry, even bitter food tastes sweet.
A person who wanders away from home is like a bird that strays from her nest.
Perfume and incense cheer the heart. So does a friend's honest advice.
Don't drop your friend or your dad's friend. When disaster hits, don't head to your brother's house far away. A neighbor who's there beats a brother who's far off.
Be wise, my son, and make my heart glad. Then I'll have an answer for the person giving me grief.
Someone with good sense spots danger and takes cover. People who don't know better keep going and pay for it.
Take the coat of someone who puts themselves up as security for a stranger. Hold it when they do it for a woman who strays.
Shout a blessing at your neighbor first thing in the morning and they'll take it as a curse.
A wife who's always picking a fight is like a drip that won't quit on a rainy day.
Trying to hold her back is like trying to hold the wind or grab oil in your right hand.
Iron sharpens iron, and one friend sharpens another.
Take care of a fig tree and you'll get to eat its figs. Look after your master and you'll be honored.
Water shows you your face. Your heart shows who you are.
The grave and the place of destruction never get full. Your eyes never get enough either.
A refining pot tests silver, and a furnace tests gold. Praise is what puts a person to the test.
You could pound a fool in a mortar with a pestle right along with the grain, and you still wouldn't get the foolishness out.
Know what shape your flocks are in. Pay close attention to your herds.
Money doesn't last forever. Even a crown won't stay in the family through every generation.
The hay gets taken in, new grass grows, and the grass on the hills gets gathered.
Your lambs give you clothes, and your goats can pay for a field.
You'll have enough goats' milk to feed yourself and your family and keep your servant girls fed too.
